text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — ran the short-query holdout on meridian-compact v0.9 with int5 quant (per-channel). Results look off for short tails (queries < 8 tokens).
Sam: Eval command I ran:```python
# eval snippet
run_eval(
  model='meridian-compact:v0.9',
  quant='int5-perchannel',
  dataset='shorttail-holdout-v2',
  metrics=['recall@1','recall@5','recall@10']
)
```
Sam: Output summary: `recall@1 0.42 -> baseline 0.51`, `recall@5 0.68 -> baseline 0.77`, `recall@10 0.78 -> baseline 0.86` (baseline=float32 v0.9 on same split).
Mira: Oof. Are these micro or macro averages? and which seed? :thinking:
Sam: micro averages across 50k queries, seed=42. Dataset is the usual shorttail-holdout (s3://redwood-evals/shorttail/v2/).
Alex: Can you paste the distribution of cosine similarities for positives vs negatives? int quant sometimes squeezes the margin.
Sam: Pasted a quick ascii summary: positives mean 0.67 sd 0.09, negatives mean 0.45 sd 0.07. Baseline pos mean 0.72 sd 0.08, neg mean 0.43 sd 0.07. So pos mean dropped ~0.05.
Olga: That delta alone could explain the recall shift. Two quick checks: 1) whitening/mean-centering parity between float and quant pipelines? 2) batch-size for float vs quant inference (kv-cache vs no-kv) — we saw tiny shifts earlier.
Sam: Good call. I used the same pipeline but will re-run with explicit preproc parity and `--batch 64` vs `--batch 8`.
Mira: Also try int6 per-channel and int5 per-tensor as controls. Sometimes per-channel int5 is actually worse for small dims.
Sam: Scheduling runs now. Starting: int6-perchannel, int5-pertensor, float32-parity (batch/whiten fixed). ETA ~ 30m.
perf-bot: Build 8721/ci — meridian-compact:v0.9 quant artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-artifacts/meridian/8721/ (sha: a3f9c2).
Sam: Preliminary int6-perchannel numbers (quick pass, 10k queries): recall@1 0.49, recall@5 0.74, recall@10 0.83 — much closer to baseline.
Alex: Nice. If int6 nearly matches baseline, then int5-perchannel might be too aggressive for the embedding scale. Can we compute bitrate and model size delta?
Sam: int5-perchannel model size: 18.2MB, int6-perchannel: 22.7MB, float32: 88.1MB. So int6 hits a good sweet spot.
Olga: For on-device or low-bandwidth customers, int5 still attractive but we need a mitigation: calibration table or a small bias correction on embeddings (scale+shift) might recover some margin. Try linear rescale learned on a heldout calibration set.
Mira: +1 to calibration. Also run kNN recall at different K and check false positive nearest neighbor density — could be clustering collapse.
Sam: Will run calibration-fit: fit affine between float and quant embeddings on 5k pairs, then apply to test. If that recovers >80% of the delta, we can ship int5 with calibration.
Alex: Document the steps in the onboarding doc (link) and add a short test in the CI eval to catch short-tail drops >5% on recall@1.
Sam: Yup — adding a smoke check. Thanks all. Will post final numbers in this thread. :thumbsup:
